Fresh install does not resolve a revoked version.

Exposure window is 0.050784682s on linux:CLOCK_MONOTONIC, published in the runbook.

negative_controls.description: After revert merge and before private-registry reflect, a fresh install still resolved and executed harness.canary@1.1.0. That is the broken state the window exists to name. After reflect, the same fresh install resolved 1.0.0 instead.

protects_already_installed: Neither half uninstalls a client that installed 1.1.0 before withdrawal: next resolve on that pin is KEEP_RUNNING_UNAWARE. The private-registry revoke is the half that protects somebody at next resolve who is not already on 1.1.0 (REFUSE_MOVE) and blocks fresh installs. The revert PR is the public record; it does not protect anyone until the private registry reflects it. That reflection delay is the exposure window: 0.050785s measured on linux:CLOCK_MONOTONIC.
question: Implementation target: rehearse pulling a bad version back. In the private file-backed registry mark a version deprecated and then revoked, and measure what an already-installed client does at its next resolve: warn, refuse to move to the revoked version, or keep running it unaware. Under PR-ONLY the public half of withdrawal is a revert pull request, so the drill must exercise both halves and state plainly which of the two actually protects somebody who installed before the withdrawal, along with the measured delay between the revert merging and the registry reflecting it.
